review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped its declarations (fourPairGood, distanceDifferenceKernel, fourSpatialPairEquiv) across the project. I read the downstream uses in PositiveDistanceRebinBound.lean and ActualComparableShellRebin.lean. The file has no simp attributes and no competing or cyclic rules. The only issue I found is a missing membership simp interface for the new definition fourPairGood. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemma and its proof are untested. I did not recommend simp on kernel-unfolding identities, because the repeated unfolding of distanceDifferenceKernel is a weaker case.

findings.declaration: PlanarFalconer.fourPairGood (missing mem_fourPairGood) and its use in original_complex_kernel_max
findings.excerpt:
def fourPairGood (G H : Set (Plane × Plane)) : Set (Fin 4 → Plane) :=
  fourSpatialPairEquiv ⁻¹' (G ×ˢ H)
findings.problem: fourPairGood is a plain def with no membership lemma. Every client that needs to reason about `x ∈ fourPairGood G H` must unfold the definition inside `simp only`. This happens at line 77 here and in PositiveDistanceRebinBound.lean at line 40. In both places the unfolding is mixed with mem_preimage, mem_inter_iff and MeasurableEquiv.symm_apply_apply. The only simp-visible form is the opaque preimage under fourSpatialPairEquiv, so the desired normal form, a conjunction of membership of (x 0, x 1) in G and (x 2, x 3) in H, is never exposed. Unfolding the def also leaves a preimage and a product set that depend on how fourSpatialPairEquiv reduces.
findings.proposed_change: Right after the def, add a membership lemma, e.g. `@[simp] theorem mem_fourPairGood {G H : Set (Plane × Plane)} {x : Fin 4 → Plane} : x ∈ fourPairGood G H ↔ (x 0, x 1) ∈ G ∧ (x 2, x 3) ∈ H := Iff.rfl`. Prove it by `Iff.rfl` or `by simp [fourPairGood, fourSpatialPairEquiv]`, after checking how fourSpatialPairEquiv is defined at lean/OAI/MeasureTheory/Falconer/Measures/FourSpatialPairMeasure.lean:10. Alternatively add a non-simp `mem_fourPairGood_iff`. The orientation is membership to a conjunction of coordinate memberships, which cannot loop. Then replace `simp only [T,mem_inter_iff,mem_preimage,fourPairGood, MeasurableEquiv.symm_apply_apply]` in the proofs of `he` with a simp call that uses the lemma. Do the same at PositiveDistanceRebinBound.lean:40, which drops `fourPairGood` from the simp set.
findings.benefit: The definition becomes a stable abstraction, so clients no longer unfold fourPairGood. Goals about membership in the good set normalize to a readable coordinate-wise conjunction. The two set-equality proofs `he` (here and in PositiveDistanceRebinBound.lean) become shorter and more robust. The change cannot loop and affects only terms of the form `_ ∈ fourPairGood _ _`.
